notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Measure a useful collector experience, then fix the friction.
intro: A proposed growth-infrastructure workbench for Trove, focused on reliable onboarding events, collection-management milestones and owned support escalation.
queueIntro: Synthetic cohort records represent groups, not identifiable users. There are no pack purchases, card valuations, odds changes or buyback transactions in this demo.
workbenchIntro: Review event quality, meaningful product use and support ownership. The experiment measures usability and user-chosen engagement, not spending intensity.
firstBuild: An activation cohort the team can trust
firstBody: Define a useful non-purchase milestone, deduplicate events and connect unresolved support issues to an owner before testing the onboarding experience.

fields.label: Acquisition source and cohort window defined
Unresolved support issue has an owner

rules.title: Define the collector cohort
rules.next: Keep install date, acquisition source and observation window consistent before comparing activation.

rules.title: Validate the event contract
rules.next: A retried event must not count as a second collector milestone. Record event names, keys and source.

rules.title: Choose an observable product milestone
rules.next: Use a meaningful collection-management or onboarding task, not spending volume, to define this pilot’s activation.

rules.title: Route the support issue first
rules.next: An account with an unresolved delivery or access issue needs support attention before engagement messaging.

rules.title: Preserve collector preferences
rules.next: Respect opt-outs and user-selected notification preferences instead of treating more messages as progress.

rules.title: Define a responsible experiment
rules.next: Measure usability and task completion alongside complaints, opt-outs and support burden. Do not optimize for excessive spending.

ready.title: Ready for an onboarding experiment review
ready.next: The team can review the cohort definition, instrumentation and user-experience guardrails before running a bounded usability test.

experiments.name: Clear collection onboarding
experiments.hypothesis: A clearer first-run guide helps users complete a chosen collection task.
experiments.primary: Unique users completing the defined non-purchase task
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Support-aware lifecycle operations
experiments.hypothesis: Owning unresolved issues improves the user experience.
experiments.treatment: Support issue reviewed before lifecycle messaging
experiments.guardrail: Repeated messages and unresolved delivery issues
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Map the collector journey and event contract
roadmap.body: Work with founders, product and support on acquisition cohorts, meaningful milestones and event definitions.

roadmap.title: Build one instrumented internal workflow
roadmap.body: Pilot an onboarding scorecard and support escalation queue with clear owners and failure visibility.
roadmap.measure: Task completion and time to owned support action

roadmap.title: Create repeatable experimentation infrastructure
roadmap.body: Compare stable cohorts, document results and make the next experiment easy to run. Keep user-experience guardrails visible.
roadmap.measure: Reliable experiments, useful retention and support quality

metricsTitle: Reliable events come before a growth conclusion.
metricsIntro: Invented onboarding cohorts use unique users and the same seven-day window.
metricsNotes: These are synthetic examples, not Trove performance or CJ’s measured results.
The milestone is collection organization, not a purchase or spending target.
A cohort difference needs uncertainty, acquisition mix and support context before it supports a rollout decision.
aiApplication: At Trove, I would apply MCP-assisted funnel analysis and bounded pipeline patterns to activation cohorts: define a useful non-purchase milestone, deduplicate events and route support blockers. Experiments would evaluate the onboarding change with clear ownership.
